questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my german skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Both the host university and my dorm provided a lot of information on their respective websites.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I did not receive any help in the beginning, but whenever I had questions, the international office was quick to answer.

The incoming mobility coordinator for my field of study was very helpful when I didn’t get a spot in one of my courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation session for all incoming students was great. It wasn’t very clear whether there was an additional orientation for my field of study. I ended up going to the orientation session for first‑year students, which provided some important (and a lot of unnecessary) information.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The host university provided a lot of information on their website for international students. I found a dorm through one of the organisations listed there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I found a dorm through the organisation WIHAST. It was a big dorm. My room was not cleaned when I moved in, but in general the place was nice and the staff were helpfull. I lived in the 19th district and even though it seemed far from the city, it only took me 30 minutes to get to the university and central spots in the city centre. 

I madetwo great friends at my dorm and was very happy that I choose this type of housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It is very important to apply for housing as early as possible. I applied in May and did not get any of my listed priorities, as those dorms were already full. However, I did get a room in a similar dorm.

When applying, I was asked to send a confirmation of enrollment at the University. Since I had not received it yet, I sent my nomination letter from my home university instead. That worked perfectly fine, and they simply asked me to send the confirmation of enrollment later.

On the dorm’s website, it appeared that it was only possible to move in at the beginning of the semester (1st of October), but in reality many people—especially exchange students—moved in on the 1st of September. So if you want to move in earlier, just write it as a comment when you apply for the dorm.
I moved in on the 1st of September, as I took a language course before the semester began.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
To me, it was difficult to figure out which courses were suitable for me. 
The Mathematics Department at Uni Wien both includes a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics and a Bachelor of Education in mathematics (a degree that makes you a primary, secondary or high school teacher). I took courses from both fields, and to me, that was a very interesting experience. 
On the other hand, I do not believe this was the most common thing to do, and one should be aware that the courses marked with BEd are similar to those from "læreruddannelsen" in Denmark.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I applied for courses in the beginning/middle of September. About a week later, it was possible to see my assigned courses on u:space. 
Be aware that you need to sign up for exercise classes and lectures separately. Exercise classes have continous assessment, and lectures end with an exam (which you also need to sign up for at the end of the semester. )

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The incoming mobility coordinator for my field of study was very helpful when I didn’t get a spot in one of my courses. He encouraged me to contact the StudienServiceCenter who secured me a spot.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was okay. I ended up getting all the courses in my learning agreement.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My impression is, that a lot of local students sign of for more courses than needed and deregister after a couple of weeks. Hence; if you do not get a spot in a course, you can show up in class the first couple of times, and ask the teacher if there is a free spot. At least three (out of 25) people in my class got a spot this way.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The workload differed a lot (also in courses that was worth the same amount of ects).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The courses were similar to danish courses in respect to difficulty. 

Most of the BA courses are held in german, and hence you should be able to understand german. I did though get the option to present in english in some of my courses, as I felt more comfortable this way. 

I took one course in english (Mathematical Logic), and my impression was, that most students in this class was exchange students. This was also by far the most difficult course and I was told, that it was structured differently that most other courses at the mathematics department.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The courses from the BEd was interesting and difficult in a different way than I am used to. The courses from BSc was very similar to those in Denmark. 
For the exercise classes you are asked to note which exercises you have succesfully solved each week, and may be asked to present those in class. The grade you recieve in based on the amount of exercises you have completed during the semester. 

You are not allowed to bring notes for the exams in Austria.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Mathematical Logic (BSc), 
Komplexe und Harmonische Analysis (BSc), 
Prakticum zum Computereinsatz im Matematikunterricht (BEd), 
Seminar zur Unterrichtsplanung (BEd), 
Summer Intensive German Course (Sprachenzentrum Uni Wien).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The language course in September was amazing. 
First of all, I got the apportunity to improve (and refresh) my German skills before the semester began, but the course also included a social programme. I went on a hike to Kahlenberg, attended two choir sessions, joined a walk in the city centre and participated in a picnic and a party. There was also an option to watch different Austrian movies and take extra German lessons in the evening. It was a very nice introduction to the city and culture of Austria.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Wifi at my dorm. But it was only 5 euros per month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was cheaper to go to a café than in Copenhagen. A cup of coffee cost about 5 euros.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I believe it possible to sign up for sports activities. But I do not believe I gout enough infomation about social clubs at the uni.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Sports activities. 
The ESN club at Uni Wien worked very well - I attended several of their events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ESN club, museums and the opera/theaters. They often have discounts for people aged under 27 or 30, or student discounts. Remember to bring your student ID.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
ESN club, museums and the opera/theaters. They often have discounts for people aged under 27 or 30, or student discounts. Remember to bring your student ID. 

Hallstatt and Bratislava should be nice to visit. I sadly didn't go to any of them. 

Christmas markets!! (Go in the end of November, not in December).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Okay. The biggest issue for me was the oppening hours of super markets, the university buildings etc. 
Everything is closed on Sundays. Supermarkes close at 7:30/8:00 pm at working days and 6:00 pm on Saturdays. 
The University buildings are also closed on Sundays.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in class and at your dorm.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Oppening hours. Always bring cash! There are still places (resturants, cafés and especially churches) that does not take card.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Christmas markets, museums and concert halls. 
The many incredible dishes, that my friends made me taste.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the registration system of courses. 
Go to the ESN events. 
Sign up for a language course.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware to type the exact adress of University buildings into Google Maps. Google Maps can not always differ between them, and the University has buildings all over the city. (I once went to the wrong building in another part of the city, 30 minutes away from the correct one....)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met. The many cultural experiences i have gotten. Not only Austrian once. Fx. I was invited to thanks giving by a friend a met at my language course.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
I missed my family and friends at home. 
I found my courses very challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Be aware that not every day will feel like an adventure. Most days will actually be quite boring and similar to your everyday life at home. But that’s okay — that is also part of the experience.
Don’t stress about having to experience something all the time. You probably need some breaks and Netflix time. I did.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
